clueShare4.paragraph: The fours file reads the same almost every night I open it. My note asked how big the four costs, not whether it exists. The range of the four's impact on time has settled on a real number, and each extra four in ten numbers adds about 5%, likely between 0.9% and 9%. This range has narrowed by 16% since July 18, and the same answer came back again, which I am listening to.

patternMoves.paragraph: Back into the pattern reasoning file, I noticed that the number I left there isn't the same as the one I found. The parked estimate moved from about 11% per ten pattern reads on Jul 13 to about 24% now. The cost comes to about 24% per ten pattern reads, with a band running from 17% to 33%. I wrote that a practiced read should cost seconds, not tens of seconds, and the data agree: the effect is real but small. A number that moves while nobody feeds it has my full attention.

mirrorPairCount.paragraph: The mirrors band is widening when it should be narrowing, according to the hypothesis I wrote that a player who spots the pair should lose almost no time. The top of the range does not read as almost no time, and the data show that the range is now 47% wider than it was on Jul 2. Ten mirror pairs add about 34% to your time, likely between 14% and 57%. Wider is still an answer, but it’s not the one I ordered.

liarCellCount.paragraph: The liar cells question got its answer. The data provided two options: poison, or a rounding error. The study covered ten study days from April 22 to June 28. The cost of liar cells was between 0% and about 3% per ten cells, which is a narrow range. I'll take a clean answer over a flattering one any day.

mysteryCellCount.paragraph: The mystery cells file closes with my prediction face-down. On study day Jun 8, the charge per ten mystery cells reads between 0% and about 3%. Most of the data arrived on ordinary boards, and I wrote that missing information has a price. I measured this price, and it turns out to be close to free. I wanted an effect, but the answer outranks the wanting.
